ruling.reasoning:
The service is a metered RydeTAXI trip: F7 shows a metered breakdown (base $3.90, distance $27.35, time $8.26, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47), so detour mileage flows into the fare and RD-2's mileage-based refund formula applies rather than the fixed-quote branch [F7][RD-2]. The code trace settles that exactly one off-route segment exists, F3 (12:29–12:39), and that no RD-4(a) incident on the replaced optimal stretch exists (F14), with the Pan Island Expressway band 2 record (F12) being corroboration only and never a standalone exemption [F3][F12][F14][RD-1][RD-4].

The only live question is RD-5 consent scope for F3. The driver asked at 12:26 whether he could "go round via Sims Avenue" (F8) and the rider answered "Sure, go ahead." at 12:27 (F9); that reply is a specific named-road authorisation, not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation, because it answers a message naming one road [F8][F9][RD-5]. Under RD-5's specified-route limb the agreement covers driving on Sims Avenue only, and the record must tie the segment to that road — a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, or a road name in a fact. F3 gives only kilometres, timing and up-to-755 m distance from the optimal route, with no road name, and no other fact ties the 12:29–12:39 path to Sims Avenue [F3][F10][RD-5]. Timing alone (12:27 before the 12:29:55 segment start) does not do that work, and the driver's post-trip assertion that the rider agreed (F11) is a claim, not rider consent [F11][RD-5]. I therefore read F3's scope as undetermined (the record cannot settle whether the agreed road is the one driven), which is the outcome the trace contemplates where nothing ties the segment to the named road [F3][F9][RD-5].

RD-3 does not change this: no stop was measured in the segment and the rider named no place of his own, so there is no rider-named stop exemption to apply [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. RD-6 is not triggered on its own terms — the only profile facts shown are the driver's 2 upheld disputes with route: 0 (F17), and profile facts cannot decide the case in any event — so no account flag attaches [F17][RD-6].

Because the undetermined RD-5 scope controls whether 3.27 km is exempt or counts, and it changes the amount, the case must go to a person rather than being auto-decided [F3][F4][RD-5][RD-2]. If the reviewer confirms the segment was not on Sims Avenue, the refund is 3.27 km × $1.4098/km = $4.61 (rate = distance fare $27.35 ÷ distance km 19.40 = $1.4098/km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]; if it confirms Sims Avenue, F3 is exempt and the outcome is no_action [RD-5]. The rider's demand for the full billed excess of $5.54 (3.93 km, F4) is not supported, since the trace counts only F3's 3.27 km and the rider's advocate conceded the 0.63 km difference is not claimed [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].
